name: Executive order of December 21, 1882 setting apart the Turtle Mountain Reservation
nations: Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa Indians
promises: The order set apart a reserve for the Turtle Mountain band of Chippewas (Royce).
The State Historical Society of North Dakota says it created a reservation of 20 townships (460,800 acres), about the size and shape of present-day Rolette County.
today: The Court of Claims held in 1974 that the executive orders of December 21, 1882 and March 29, 1884 did not extinguish Chippewa aboriginal title, since nothing showed Congress authorized it or that the Chippewas accepted the reservation as a settlement of their claims. The Indian Claims Commission then valued 8,104,040 acres as taken on February 15, 1905 under the McCumber Agreement of October 22, 1892, as amended by the Act of April 21, 1904 (33 Stat. 189, 193), at $53,527,225.00 against $999,887.03 paid, held that consideration unconscionable, and found the plaintiffs entitled to $52,527,337.97 less offsets (September 20, 1978). That finding concerns the 1904 to 1905 taking, a separate record.

openQuestions: This order created a reservation; the Court of Claims found it did not take the band's title, and no finding treats it as a breach. The loss of most of it came by the order of March 29, 1884 (its own record) and the McCumber Agreement.
Sources differ on the size: the State Historical Society says 20 townships, other accounts say 22. Royce gives the bounds but not a count.
The Turtle Mountain Band's own website (tmbci.org) did not load, so the nation's account is missing.
